title: BILINGUAL SPANISH Customer Service Representative
description:
Customer Experience Representative (VA) – Call Center



Who We Are?

Trojan Storage is the best self-storage operator in the business with over 50+ locations in the U.S today! Simply put, we have the best people in the workplace with our amazing culture, healthy benefits, and growth opportunities.



Work Schedule

40 Hour Work Weeks | 5 Days | 8 Hours per day

11:00 PM – 8:00 AM Philippine Time (PHT), Monday through Saturday, to align with the Company's normal business hours of 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM Pacific Time (California).

Sunday Schedule: 11:30 PM – 8:00 AM PHT to align with California's Sunday business hours of 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM PT.

The work schedule may be adjusted by one hour during U.S. Daylight Saving Time changes to maintain alignment with California business hours.



Join our amazing call center today! The Customer Experience Representative (CXR) is an independent contractor that will report directly to the Contact Center Manager. This individual will play an integral role in executing the overall growth and customer service strategy of Trojan Storage. The CXR will be the front line for new customers’ rentals as well as handling a variety of customer issues utilizing phone, SMS, chat, and
. The CXR must possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills, as well as be enthusiastic about helping customers and driving satisfaction.



Your Responsibilities:

• Customer Experience: Delight customers through multichannel communications including phone,
, chat, and video. Become proficient in self-storage operations delivering empathetic communications to all our customers practicing First Contact Resolution (FCR). Handle and mitigate customer complaints with effective communication and proper documentation.

• Collections: Take payments and assist customers with all delinquency needs ensuring proper documentation and compliance.

• Efficiency: Drive performance through keeping efficiency ratios at standards. This includes managing average handle times, response times, and calls handled per day.

• Teamwork: Foster positive relationships with team members and leadership collaborating effectively on initiatives, meetings, and daily interactions.

• Punctuality & Attendance: Adhere to all schedules and meetings on time with no disruption to the contact center environment. Be a reliable team member to support operational efficiency and team cohesion.

• Interpersonal Skills: Communicate effectively with all internal stakeholders such as site personnel, District Managers, and within the contact center.



Qualifications

• Senior High School diploma or equivalent required.

• 1 Year of experience in a contact center environment or customer-support role

• Phone sales experience 

• Bilingual (Spanish and English) required.

• Proficiency in chat communication a plus.

• Ability to multi-task and manage time effectively.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• Experience in conflict resolution 



Apply today to join one of the fastest growing self-storage operators in the business!



Independent Contractor Disclaimer



This opportunity is for an Independent Contractor (Virtual Assistant) position and is not an employment position with Andasol Management Inc. dba Trojan Storage or any of its affiliated companies. Services will be performed pursuant to an Independent Contractor Agreement, and nothing in this job posting or any subsequent agreement shall be construed as creating an employer-employee relationship. As an independent contractor, you will be responsible for all applicable taxes, government contributions, permits, insurance, and compliance with the laws and regulations of your country of residence. Independent contractors are not eligible for employee benefits, including but not limited to paid holidays, paid time off, overtime pay, sick leave, health benefits, retirement benefits, or 13th month pay.



This engagement is designed to provide full-time work of approximately 40 hours per week, with a regular schedule of Monday through Friday during the Philippine time zone, supporting U.S. Pacific Time business operations. From time to time, contractors may be required to attend virtual team meetings or training sessions that occur during U.S. business hours. Advance notice will be provided whenever reasonably possible to allow for scheduling.



Independent contractors are responsible for providing and maintaining their own computer, reliable high-speed internet connection, backup power and internet solutions (when feasible), and a professional, dedicated workspace suitable for conducting business. Andasol Management Inc. will provide a company-issued headset for business use.



Contractors are required to accurately record all hours worked using the Company's designated timekeeping platform, TimeProof. Compensation is paid bi-weekly on Tuesdays, provided the payment date does not fall on a U.S. holiday. The pay period consists of two consecutive workweeks beginning Sunday and ending Saturday. Contractors must submit their invoice for the completed pay period no later than 12:00 PM Pacific Time on the Tuesday immediately following the close of the pay period. Approved invoices will be processed for payment on that same day. Payments are issued through Payoneer.

title: Appointment Setter – Warm Window Replacement Leads (US) | Full-Time & Part-Time
description:
Pareto Home (US window replacement) is hiring 2–6 appointment setters to call homeowners who already asked for a quote. No cold lists. You call warm leads, handle a few objections, and book a free in-home measurement for our sales team.



THE ROLE

• 150+ outbound calls per shift on our dialer

• Book qualified measurement appointments and log every call in the CRM

• Monday–Friday, US Pacific daytime hours (exact shift confirmed at hire)

• Full-time (40 hrs) or part-time (20 hrs). Long-term. Start ASAP.

• Up to $4.50/hr based on experience, paid weekly



REQUIREMENTS

• 1+ year of outbound calling to US customers (appointment setting, cold calling, or telesales). Customer service or admin experience alone does not qualify.

• Clear, confident spoken English

• Quiet workspace, headset, wired internet with backup, backup power

• Has used a dialer (CallTools, Mojo, Convoso, Five9, etc.) and a CRM

• Bonus: home services (windows, roofing, HVAC, solar) or GoHighLevel



HOW TO APPLY – applications missing any of these will be skipped

1. Start your message with the word WINDOWS

2. Say full-time or part-time

3. Attach a 60–90 second voice recording: your name and age, your outbound calling experience, whether you currently have another job, and why you're a fit

4. Google Drive link only, set to "Anyone with the link." No Vocaroo.

5. Highest calls per day you've handled, and in what industry



Shortlisted applicants get a 15-minute video interview with a short role-play call.

We are seeking an experienced, proactive, and highly organized Credentialing and Provider/Practice Enrollment Specialist to manage the credentialing, enrollment, recredentialing, and licensing requirements of our growing multi-location vascular medical practice in Orange County, California.



This position encompasses individual provider credentialing, group and practice enrollment, Office-Based Lab (OBL) enrollment and credentialing, insurance address and practice location management, and administrative company licensing, registrations, and renewals.



The ideal candidate must have solid, hands-on experience with the end-to-end credentialing and enrollment process and be capable of independently managing applications, identifying required documentation, communicating with insurance companies and regulatory agencies, and resolving outstanding issues.



We are looking for someone who already understands the credentialing process, knows whom to contact, understands what documentation is required, and can proactively resolve issues without requiring constant supervision or step-by-step instructions.



Key Responsibilities



1. Provider Credentialing and Enrollment



* Manage the end-to-end credentialing and enrollment process for physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and other healthcare providers.

* Prepare, complete, and submit credentialing and enrollment applications to insurance companies, health plans, hospitals, and other relevant organizations.

* Coordinate provider enrollment with Medicare, Medi-Cal, and commercial insurance payers.

* Manage initial credentialing, recredentialing, reenrollment, revalidation, and provider information updates.

* Manage provider affiliations, group linkages, and reassignment of benefits, as applicable.

* Maintain and update provider profiles in CAQH, NPPES, PECOS, and other applicable credentialing platforms.

* Coordinate hospital privileging and reappointments, as applicable.

* Verify credentialing approvals, effective dates, network participation, and applicable billing eligibility.





2. Group, Practice, and Organizational Enrollment



* Manage credentialing and enrollment requirements for group practices and organizational entities.

* Coordinate group and practice enrollment with Medicare, Medi-Cal, and commercial insurance payers.

* Manage organizational NPI registrations, group enrollment records, and applicable TIN-related updates.

* Coordinate the addition and removal of providers under existing group and practice enrollments.

* Manage group revalidation, reenrollment, and organizational information updates.

* Assist with payer contracting, participation agreements, and network enrollment requirements.

* Ensure that organizational and provider affiliations are accurately reflected in payer systems.



3. Practice Location and Insurance Address Management



* Manage the addition, removal, relocation, and updating of practice locations with insurance companies and relevant agencies.

* Maintain accurate service, billing, mailing, and pay-to addresses across applicable enrollment systems.

* Ensure providers are appropriately affiliated with their designated practice locations.

* Maintain accurate practice and provider information across insurance directories, payer portals, and credentialing databases.

* Identify and resolve discrepancies involving practice addresses, provider information, and organizational records.

* Follow up on submitted changes and verify that updates have been successfully processed.



4. Office-Based Lab (OBL) and Facility-Related Credentialing and Enrollment



* Manage applicable credentialing and enrollment requirements for the practice’s Office-Based Lab (OBL) and other clinical or procedural locations.

* Identify and research payer-specific and regulatory requirements related to OBL enrollment and operations.

* Coordinate provider, organizational, and service location enrollment requirements associated with the OBL.

* Assist with applicable facility licensing, permits, certifications, accreditation, and regulatory documentation.

* Verify applicable provider and payer enrollment requirements for services performed at the OBL.

* Communicate with insurance companies, regulatory agencies, and accreditation organizations regarding facility-related requirements.

* Monitor applicable OBL licenses, certifications, accreditation, and renewal deadlines.



5. Administrative Licensing, Registration, and Renewals



* Manage and coordinate company, practice, and facility-related license applications, registrations, permits, and renewals.

* Assist with obtaining and maintaining applicable business licenses, operational permits, certifications, and other regulatory documentation.

* Coordinate provider medical license, DEA registration, professional certification, and other applicable renewals.

* Maintain accurate records of company, practice, facility, and provider licenses and expiration dates.

* Proactively identify upcoming renewal requirements, necessary documentation, fees, and deadlines.

* Communicate directly with government agencies, licensing boards, regulatory organizations, and other relevant representatives.

* Independently research application procedures and requirements for new licenses, registrations, permits, and renewals.

* Provide administrative support for company-related applications and regulatory documentation as assigned.



6. Documentation and Verification



* Independently identify, collect, review, and organize required credentialing, enrollment, and licensing documentation.

* Verify provider licenses, certifications, education, training, work history, and professional qualifications.

* Maintain accurate and updated provider, group, practice, and facility records.

* Monitor expiration dates for licenses, certifications, malpractice insurance, accreditation, and other required documents.

* Proactively obtain missing or incomplete documentation.

* Maintain organized electronic records of applications, approvals, correspondence, and supporting documentation.

* Ensure confidential provider and organizational information is handled securely.



7. Insurance, Payer, and Regulatory Agency Coordination



* Communicate directly with insurance companies, credentialing departments, provider enrollment representatives, licensing boards, and regulatory agencies.

* Identify the appropriate departments, representatives, and escalation channels for specific inquiries.

* Proactively follow up on pending applications, approvals, renewals, and outstanding updates.

* Resolve application discrepancies, missing information, enrollment issues, and processing delays.

* Coordinate with billing, eligibility, authorizations, and other internal departments regarding credentialing and enrollment-related concerns.

* Obtain confirmation of approvals, effective dates, participation status, and completed updates.

* Maintain accurate records of correspondence, reference numbers, and follow-up activities.



8. Tracking, Deadline Management, and Reporting



* Maintain a comprehensive tracker covering provider credentialing, group and practice enrollment, practice locations, OBL requirements, and administrative licenses.

* Track application statuses, submission dates, follow-up dates, effective dates, expiration dates, and renewal deadlines.

* Manage multiple applications and assignments simultaneously while ensuring accuracy and timely completion.

* Establish advance reminders for upcoming expirations, recredentialing, revalidation, and renewals.

* Proactively escalate delays or issues that may affect provider start dates, billing eligibility, practice operations, or regulatory compliance.

* Provide regular progress reports to management regarding pending applications, completed tasks, outstanding requirements, and potential risks.

* Recommend improvements to streamline credentialing, enrollment, and administrative workflows.



Qualifications and Requirements



* At least two years of direct, hands-on experience in medical credentialing and provider enrollment.

* Strong working knowledge of the complete, end-to-end credentialing and enrollment process.

* Experience handling individual provider and group practice credentialing and enrollment.

* Experience with Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial insurance payer enrollment.

* Strong familiarity with CAQH, NPPES, PECOS, and commercial payer credentialing and enrollment portals.

* Knowledge of individual and organizational NPI registrations, group affiliations, and provider enrollment updates.

* Experience managing practice location additions, insurance address changes, and provider directory updates.

* Knowledge of required credentialing documentation and verification procedures.

* Experience communicating directly with insurance companies, payer enrollment departments, and relevant agencies.

* Ability to independently research and understand unfamiliar licensing, enrollment, and administrative requirements.

* Strong analytical, problem-solving, follow-up, and deadline management skills.

* Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

* Highly organized, detail-oriented, proactive, reliable, and efficient.

* Ability to manage multiple applications and administrative assignments independently with minimal supervision.

* Proficient in Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, spreadsheets, and credentialing databases.





Preferred Qualifications



* Experience working with California-based healthcare organizations.

* Familiarity with California Medi-Cal enrollment through PAVE.

* Experience working with multi-location medical practices or specialty healthcare organizations.

* Experience with vascular practices, Office-Based Labs (OBLs), Ambulatory Surgery Centers (ASCs), or other outpatient procedural settings.

* Experience with facility enrollment, licensing, accreditation, and regulatory requirements.

* Experience with hospital credentialing, privileging, and reappointments.

* Experience managing company licenses, business permits, facility registrations, and administrative renewals.

* Familiarity with payer contracting, network participation, and credentialing-related claim denials.



What We Are Looking For



We are looking for someone who:



* Takes full ownership of assigned responsibilities from initiation through completion.

* Can work independently without requiring constant supervision or step-by-step instructions.

* Knows how to identify requirements, locate the appropriate contacts, and determine the correct application procedures.

* Proactively follows up on applications and outstanding requirements without needing repeated reminders.

* Demonstrates initiative in researching unfamiliar processes and identifying effective solutions.

* Communicates concerns, delays, and potential risks to management in a timely manner.

* Maintains a high level of accuracy, accountability, professionalism, and attention to detail.



The successful candidate must be able to manage credentialing, enrollment, and licensing responsibilities efficiently while ensuring that all assigned applications, updates, and renewals are completed accurately and within required timelines.

title: Planning & Forecast Analyst - OTB and Replenishment
description:
About the Role

We are a jewelry and accessories brand operating across DTC and Amazon channels, looking for a Planning & Forecast Analyst to own our OTB Planner and turn SKU-level forecasts into confident monthly replenishment buys.



Our OTB Planner was built in Claude and went live recently — it produces the numbers, and this role makes sure they’re right, explains what they mean, and improves the logic as we learn where it’s strong and where it misses. This is half analyst, half model builder: you’ll review every cycle’s output and challenge outliers, then build and ship the logic changes yourself directly in Claude.



Our business runs on thousands of SKUs, many of which launch strong and fade quickly — making demand hard to predict. This role exists to model those launch-and-fade patterns and keep the buy right across the whole assortment.



Work Structure & Requirements



🏠 Location: Remote / Virtual (Philippines)

📅 Schedule: Full-time

🌏 Time Zone: EST — available 8:00 AM–2:00 PM Eastern for live collaboration with the team

💵 Compensation: $12–$15 USD per hour



Key Responsibilities



1. Monthly Replenishment Cycle



Run the OTB Planner each month and prepare the recommended replenishment buy for DTC and Amazon

Review SKU-level forecasts line by line before they become POs; flag and resolve outliers

Reconcile the SKU-level buy back to the OTB dollar plan by channel, category, and month



2. Data Analysis



Separate DTC and Amazon demand drivers — promotions, traffic, FBA constraints, seasonality, gifting peaks

Identify at-risk SKUs early: projected stockouts, overstock, and slow movers

Build simple, repeatable views that show the buy, the risks, and what changed since last month



3. Model Logic & Development



Model launch and fade curves: how fast new SKUs ramp, when they peak, and when to stop rebuying

Design and build logic updates (seasonality weights, safety stock, lead times, new-item and end-of-life rules, channel splits) backed by evidence

Back-test every change against recent history, get sign-off, roll it out, and roll it back if it underperforms

Version and document every logic change so the team always knows what the model is doing and why



4. Communication & Reporting



Present the monthly buy recommendation with a short read on risks and changes

Answer “why is the model saying this?” for merchandising, eCommerce, and Amazon partners

Lead weekly model reviews covering what sold vs. forecast, which SKUs are being missed, and what logic changes to test next



Required Skills & Experience



⚠️ AI Fluency: Works in Claude day-to-day to run, question, and update the planner — this is core to the role, not a nice-to-have

⚠️ Quantitative Skills: Strong math and modeling background — forecasting, statistics, and building and stress-testing model logic

Data: Comfortable working with large SKU-level datasets in Excel or Google Sheets

Attention to Detail: Catches the outlier SKU before it becomes a bad PO

Communication: Explains numbers clearly to merchants, eCommerce, and Amazon partners

Adaptability: Comfortable as the model, priorities, and data evolve month to month

Business Curiosity: Checks whether a number makes sense for the business, not just whether the math is right

Background: Analytics, finance/FP&A, data science, economics, or a similar quantitative field — retail planning experience helpful but not required



Nice to Have



Retail planning experience (OTB, replenishment, weeks of supply)

Amazon Seller/Vendor Central experience (FBA inventory, in-stock, replenishment)

DTC / Shopify eCommerce experience

Experience forecasting short-lifecycle or high-SKU-count products

Jewelry, accessories, or fashion retail background



To Apply:

Kindly send your resume and introduction video

title: Admin Operations & Media Specialist
PUBLISHING PRODUCTION COORDINATOR
description:
STANDARDS:

If you can commit to and live with the following principles, then you are the type of person who will be successful and help our company thrive. If you feel this level of engagement is not right for you or that you’re not willing or able to participate with us at this level, we are not a good fit for you.



Our expectation is that you will take the steps necessary to do what you say you are going to do and be accountable for your actions. You are committed to excellence and take pride in a job well done.



We understand that not every person is ready for this level of performance, and we appreciate the honesty of those who d
 this is not the right place for them. On the other hand, you would make an ideal candidate to join our company if you are willing to commit to the following principles:

·         Accountability: See It, Own It, Solve It, Do It

·         Become part of the solution

·         Respect for others and their feelings

·         Act now.

·         Ask the question: “What else can I do?”

·         Ask the questions: “What coaching do you have for me” and “What can I do better?”

·         Personal ownership and pride

·         Reject average

·         Show others that you care



GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF POSITION

Laurel Elite Books is seeking an experienced Publishing Production Coordinator to coordinate and execute the day-to-day production of our books from manuscript handoff through publication and launch.



This is an execution, coordination, and follow-through role requiring prior professional publishing experience.



The Publishing Production Coordinator works closely with the Production Editor, who owns the overall production plan, timelines, technical publishing decisions, specifications, and quality standards.



The Production Coordinator is responsible for making that plan happen.



The successful candidate must bring a working understanding of book-production workflows, strong project-management skills, exceptional attention to detail, proactive communication, and the ability to keep multiple projects moving without requiring constant oversight.



We provide training in our company's systems, procedures, and standards. We do not provide foundational training in how book publishing works.



The Production Coordinator does not independently determine publishing strategy or make specialized technical publishing decisions. However, they must possess sufficient industry experience to understand the production process, recognize missing information or risks, execute established instructions accurately, and escalate matters requiring decisions.



Core principle: The Production Editor owns the plan. The Production Coordinator owns the execution of the plan.



IMPORTANT: THIS IS NOT A BOOK OR MANUSCRIPT EDITING ROLE



This is a publishing production and project coordination position, not a manuscript editing position. Experience in book or manuscript editing alone is not sufficient to qualify for this role.

While manuscript editing is one component of the publishing process, coordinating the production of a book requires a substantially different set of skills, knowledge, and professional experience.



A manuscript editor focuses primarily on the content and quality of a manuscript. A Publishing Production Coordinator is responsible for the operational execution of the entire book-production process, from manuscript handoff through publication and launch.



This requires practical experience with:

- Production workflows: Understanding how copyediting, proofreading, author approvals, cover design, interior formatting, proof production, distribution, and publication fit together.

- Project management: Coordinating multiple books, contributors, deadlines, deliverables, and dependencies simultaneously.

Publishing operations: Working with ISBNs, metadata, publication files, distribution requirements, and platforms such as Amazon KDP and IngramSpark.

- Contributor coordination: Managing handoffs between authors, editors, designers, formatters, and other publishing professionals, ensuring that each stage is completed before the next begins.

- Quality control: Verifying that files, specifications, approvals, and publication information are accurate and complete before work moves forward.

- Independent execution: Following established production plans, anticipating obstacles, resolving routine operational issues, and escalating decisions appropriately without requiring constant direction.



Knowing how to edit a manuscript does not mean knowing how to produce and publish a book. These are distinct professional competencies.



We are not seeking someone who hopes to transition from manuscript editing into publishing production and learn the fundamentals while performing the job. We are seeking someone who already possesses the necessary publishing-production experience and can apply that knowledge immediately.



Laurel Elite Books provides training in our specific systems, procedures, and standards. We do not provide foundational training in the publishing-production profession.



Candidates whose professional experience is limited to manuscript editing, without demonstrated hands-on experience coordinating the broader book-production process, will not meet the minimum qualifications for this position.



PRIMARY DUTIES

1. Execute the Production Plan

For every assigned title:

- Work from the production plan and timeline established by the Production Editor.

- Translate established plans into clear, trackable tasks.

- Ensure tasks, deadlines, owners, and dependencies are accurately reflected in the project-management system.

- Coordinate each stage of production.

- Understand how editorial, design, formatting, proofing, distribution, and publication stages depend on one another.

- Ensure work moves from one production stage to the next without unnecessary delay.

- Follow up on outstanding deliverables without waiting for reminders.

- Confirm completion rather than assuming completion.

- Keep project information accurate and current.

- Immediately flag anything that threatens the established production schedule.

- Identify and initiate the next established step without requiring the Production Editor to direct routine actions individually.



Definition of Done: The production plan established by the Production Editor is accurately executed, tracked, and completed without the Production Editor or CEO having to chase routine tasks.



2. Coordinate Contributors and Deliverables

Coordinate the day-to-day work required from:

- Authors

- Editors

- Proofreaders

- Cover designers

- Interior designers and formatters

- Audiobook vendors

- Marketing contributors

- Other production vendors and contractors

- Responsibilities include:

- Sending established instructions and materials.

- Confirming receipt.

- Tracking deadlines.

- Following up before deadlines become problems.

- Collecting completed deliverables.

- Checking that deliverables meet established submission requirements.

- Routing deliverables to the correct person or next production stage.

- Ensuring required approvals are obtained.

- Maintaining organized project files.

- Documenting decisions and project status.

- Identifying when a contributor's delay affects another contributor or production milestone.

- Following outstanding work through to resolution rather than considering the task complete when a message has been sent.

- The Production Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that handoffs actually happen.



Definition of Done: Everyone involved in the project knows what they are responsible for, has what they need, and delivers according to the established schedule.



3. Maintain Production Timelines and Project Tracking

The Production Editor establishes and owns the overall production timeline.

The Production Coordinator maintains and executes it.

This includes:

- Keeping project-management systems current.

- Updating deadlines and task status.

- Tracking dependencies across multiple active titles.

- Identifying upcoming deadlines.

- Following up with responsible parties.

- Recording changes approved by the Production Editor.

- Providing accurate project-status information.

- Identifying stalled or at-risk work.

- Escalating risks before they affect publication dates.

- Monitoring work proactively rather than relying on reminders or status requests.

- Identifying when a missing deliverable will affect a later stage, even when the immediate deadline has not yet passed.

- Maintaining sufficient visibility that the Production Editor can assess the entire production pipeline without reconstructing project status.

- A deadline should never pass unnoticed.



Definition of Done: At any point, the company can see exactly where every book stands, what happens next, who owns it, and whether anything is at risk.



4. Execute Publishing and Distribution Tasks

The Production Coordinator executes publishing decisions and specifications established or approved by the Production Editor.

This may include:

- Preparing and organizing files for publication.

- Entering and updating metadata.

- Uploading files and information to Amazon KDP, IngramSpark, and other approved platforms.

- Implementing approved pricing.

- Implementing approved formats and distribution settings.

- Obtaining ISBNs and maintaining publication records.

- Coordinating proofs.

- Ordering and tracking proof copies.

- Making approved platform updates.

- Confirming that changes have been implemented correctly.

- Maintaining accurate records of final publication information.

- Recognizing routine platform requirements, file requirements, and publishing terminology.

- Identifying discrepancies between approved specifications and information entered into publication platforms.

- Investigating routine technical or procedural obstacles using available documentation and established support resources before escalating.

- The Production Coordinator is expected to understand publishing operations well enough to implement established decisions accurately, rather than learning the basic publishing process while executing live client projects.



Definition of Done: Approved publication specifications are implemented correctly, completely, and on schedule.



5. Perform First-Level Quality Control

The Production Coordinator performs operational quality checks before deliverables move forward.

This includes:

- Confirming correct files and versions are being used.

- Checking that required components are present.

- Comparing deliverables against established checklists and specifications.

- Confirming metadata has been entered accurately.

- Verifying links, files, uploads, and platform information.

- Identifying obvious errors, inconsistencies, or missing elements.

- Returning incomplete work when established requirements have not been met.

- Routing items requiring technical or professional judgment to the Production Editor.

- Checking that instructions have been fully implemented before reporting completion.

- Catching discrepancies that would otherwise require the Production Editor or CEO to repeat routine checks.

- The Production Coordinator does not replace professional editors, proofreaders, designers, or the Production Editor's final technical QC.



Definition of Done: Routine errors and omissions are caught before they reach the Production Editor, CEO, author, or marketplace.



6. Manage Routine Author Production Communication

Serve as a day-to-day point of coordination for routine production matters.

This includes:

- Requesting materials.

- Communicating established deadlines.

- Sending instructions.

- Following up on outstanding items.

- Confirming receipt of materials.

- Providing routine status updates.

- Coordinating approvals and proofs.

- Answering procedural questions covered by existing systems and SOPs.

- Anticipating routine questions and providing complete instructions so authors and contributors can act without unnecessary exchanges.

- Ensuring communications produce the required next action or identifying promptly when they do not.

- Questions requiring publishing expertise beyond the coordinator's authority, exceptions to established policy, strategic decisions, or changes to the production plan should be routed to the Production Editor.



Definition of Done: Authors receive clear, timely communication and know what is required of them throughout production.



7. Maintain Production SOPs and Documentation

The Production Editor determines or approves production standards and processes.

The Production Coordinator helps ensure those systems remain usable and current by:

- Documenting established processes.

- Updating SOPs when approved processes change.

- Maintaining checklists and templates.

- Identifying missing or unclear documentation.

- Flagging recurring operational problems.

- Ensuring current procedures are followed consistently.

- Reviewing the relevant SOP and project records before asking for procedural guidance.

- Distinguishing between genuinely missing instructions and information already available in company documentation.

- Proposing improvements for approval rather than independently changing established production systems.

- The Production Coordinator should identify opportunities for improvement and bring them forward rather than independently changing established production systems.



Definition of Done: The documented process reflects the actual approved process, and routine work can be executed consistently from it.



ESCALATION EXPECTATIONS

This role is not expected to know everything.

It is expected to arrive with foundational publishing knowledge, exercise independent judgment within established authority, and recognize when something requires clarification or escalation.

When an issue arises:

1. Identify exactly what is blocking progress.

2. Review the relevant project information, SOP, prior decisions, and available documentation.

3. Investigate the issue using appropriate resources rather than immediately transferring the problem to a supervisor.

4. Determine what can be handled independently within established procedures.

5. If a decision is required, escalate it to the Production Editor with the relevant context, actions already taken, and the specific decision needed.

6. Whenever possible, provide a proposed next step rather than simply presenting a problem.

7. Continue moving every unaffected portion of the project forward.

8. Follow through on the response or decision until the required outcome is verified.



“I don't know” begins the investigation. It does not end the assignment.

Likewise, waiting silently for an answer is not an acceptable project-management strategy.

An escalation should make it easier for the Production Editor to make a decision, not require the Production Editor to investigate the issue from the beginning.



HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

You will:

- Keep books moving efficiently through production.

- Turn production plans into completed work.

- Create reliable handoffs between contributors.

- Prevent routine details from becoming production emergencies.

- Maintain accurate and useful project information.

- Catch missing pieces before they become problems.

- Resolve routine operational obstacles within established authority.

- Anticipate next steps and dependencies.

- Reduce the amount of follow-up, checking, and supervision required from leadership.

- Free the Production Editor to focus on technical oversight, planning, and publishing expertise.

- Free the CEO from day-to-day production execution.

- Your success is measured by whether projects move smoothly and accurately without unnecessary intervention from leadership.

- The position exists to increase operational capacity. Successful performance means that assigning work to the coordinator reduces the workload of the Production Editor and CEO rather than creating additional work through repeated instruction, preventable corrections, or unresolved follow-up.



REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Professional Publishing Experience — Mandatory

Candidates must have demonstrated professional experience in book publishing or book-production coordination.

This experience must include practical familiarity with:

- The stages of book production, from manuscript handoff through publication.

- Editorial workflows, including copyediting, proofreading, author review, and approvals.

- Cover design, interior formatting, and production-file handoffs.

- Production timelines, dependencies, and contributor coordination.

- ISBNs, metadata, formats, and distribution requirements.

- Publication platforms and processes, including Amazon KDP, IngramSpark, or comparable publishing systems.

- The operational requirements of bringing a book to publication.



Candidates must be able to explain what they personally executed, not merely identify publishing terminology or describe work completed by others.



Experience solely in manuscript editing, writing, general administration, or marketing does not, by itself, satisfy the publishing-production experience requirement.



We will provide training in Laurel Elite Books' specific systems, standards, and procedures. We expect candidates to arrive with the industry foundation necessary to use that training immediately and productively.



Project Management and Operational Execution — Mandatory

- Experience coordinating multi-stage projects and deadlines.

- Strong organizational and project-management skills.

- Exceptional attention to detail.

- Ability to manage multiple active projects simultaneously.

- Demonstrated ownership of tasks through verified completion.

- Ability to identify dependencies, anticipate delays, and follow up proactively.

- Ability to maintain accurate, current project records.

- Strong written communication skills.

- Ability to follow established processes accurately.

- Ability to distinguish routine execution from decisions requiring approval.

- Comfort working with Google Docs, Google Sheets, project-management systems, and online platforms.

- Ability to investigate obstacles independently and present decision-ready escalations.

- Ability to work with limited supervision while maintaining established quality standards.



Professional Attributes — Mandatory

- Ownership and follow-through

- You take responsibility for the outcome of an assignment, not merely for performing an individual action. You recognize that sending a reminder, requesting a file, or updating a task is not the same as achieving the required result.

- Independent thinking and resourcefulness

- You use the information, tools, and resources available to you. When you encounter an obstacle, you investigate, identify what can still move forward, and determine the appropriate next step. You do not require someone else to work through every routine problem for you.

- Proactive execution

- You anticipate what needs to happen next. You recognize upcoming deadlines, missing information, and dependencies before they become emergencies. You do not wait for a supervisor to discover that work has stalled.

- Accuracy and commitment to quality

- You understand that professional publishing requires accuracy, consistency, and attention to detail. You verify your work against established requirements before reporting it complete. You accept that work must meet the required standard before it can move forward.

- Accountability and coachability

- You accept feedback, correct errors, and apply what you have learned consistently. You distinguish between learning a company's particular processes and lacking the foundational expertise required to perform the job.

- Sound judgment and respect for authority

- You act independently within your assigned responsibilities while recognizing when technical, strategic, financial, or policy decisions require the Production Editor's approval. You do not confuse initiative with permission to change established decisions.

- Clear, decision-ready communication

- You communicate concisely and specifically. When escalating an issue, you explain the problem, its impact, what you have already investigated, and the decision or assistance required.

- Professional reliability

- You maintain commitments, communicate potential delays early, and ensure that deadlines, deliverables, and follow-ups do not disappear from view.



THIS POSITION IS FOR YOU IF:

You already understand how books move through professional production.

You have personally coordinated publishing deliverables and deadlines.

You naturally keep track of moving pieces.

You notice when something hasn't happened.

You follow up without being asked.

You like turning plans into completed work.

You are comfortable working from systems and checklists.

You investigate obstacles before escalating.

You communicate clearly when something is blocked.

You understand the difference between needing a decision and needing to take action.

You take responsibility for getting work across the finish line.

You ask informed questions rather than transferring unprocessed problems to someone else.

You care deeply about accuracy and quality.

You can accept feedback and apply corrections without repeated reminders.

You find satisfaction in making complex operations run smoothly behind the scenes.

THIS POSITION IS NOT FOR YOU IF:

You are looking for your first opportunity to learn how book publishing works.

Your experience is limited to manuscript editing without practical book-production coordination.

You expect extensive training in foundational publishing concepts.

You wait for someone to remind you about deadlines.

You consider sending an
 equivalent to completing the outcome.

You allow work to stall while waiting for a response.

You routinely escalate questions without first reviewing available information.

You need leadership to track your tasks for you.

You repeatedly need instructions for routine next steps.

You make technical or strategic decisions outside your authority rather than escalating them.

You consider incomplete or inaccurate work acceptable because you are still learning.

You are uncomfortable following established processes and standards.

You identify problems without helping move them toward resolution.

You require ongoing supervision that increases rather than reduces the workload of the Production Editor or CEO.



REPORTING & WORKING RELATIONSHIP

The Publishing Production Coordinator works under the direction of the Production Editor for production planning, publishing standards, technical decisions, and project priorities.

The Production Coordinator is responsible for the day-to-day execution, coordination, tracking, communication, and follow-through necessary to carry those plans through completion.

The intended workflow is:

Production Editor determines and plans → Production Coordinator coordinates and executes → Production Editor provides technical oversight and final QC.

The CEO should become involved only when a matter requires executive-level strategy, approval, or authority that falls outside the Production Editor's scope.

The working relationship depends on clear accountability:

The Production Editor provides the approved plan, standards, and technical direction.

The Production Coordinator translates that direction into organized, verified execution.

The Production Coordinator raises risks and decision points promptly, with sufficient information to enable action.

The Production Editor does not need to manage every routine task or independently discover stalled work.

The CEO is not expected to serve as the coordinator's publishing trainer, task tracker, or routine problem-solver.



The standard is not simply that the coordinator is busy or trying to help. The standard is that the coordinator's work demonstrably advances production, meets quality requirements, and reduces the operational burden on leadership.

title: AI Animation Video Creator — 3D Cartoon / Pixar-Style Social Media Videos
description:
Do you want to create beautiful AI-animated videos that reach millions of people while being part of a fast-growing music, transformation, and sound healing brand?



Our content averages roughly **50–150 million views per month**, and we're looking for a talented **AI Animation Video Creator** to join our creative team.



We already have successful scripts, voiceovers, and proven social media content. We're looking for someone who can **transform these into engaging, high-quality AI-animated videos** with a Pixar-inspired, 3D cartoon, or cinematic animation style.



**This is not a traditional video editing role.**



We're looking for someone who understands AI animation, visual storytelling, and how to create videos that capture attention and keep people watching.



## About Us



Harmony is a fast-growing transformation, music, and sound healing company founded by musician and intuitive guide Banah Winn.



We create Golden Ratio Frequencies, guided experiences, educational content, live events, and an online community dedicated to helping people create meaningful change in their lives.



Our content reaches **50–150 million views per month** across social media. We have an established creative team and a library of proven, high-performing content that we want to bring to life through animation.



## About the Role



Your main responsibility will be to **take our existing scripts, voiceovers, and winning videos and turn them into compelling AI-animated content** for Instagram,
, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts.



We'll provide the scripts, audio, and creative references.



Your job is to d
 how to visually bring them to life.



You'll be responsible for:



- Turning existing voiceovers and scripts into fully animated videos

- Creating engaging 3D cartoon characters, scenes, and environments

- Developing visual concepts that illustrate what's being said

- Matching animation timing and scene changes to the voiceover

- Creating strong visual hooks in the opening seconds

- Maintaining character and visual consistency across scenes

- Using expressions, movement, and visual storytelling to bring the message to life

- Editing animated scenes together with voiceovers, music, and sound effects

- Creating multiple visual variations of proven scripts when needed



**The goal is to take content we already know performs and give it a completely new visual format through animation.**



## What We're Looking For



- **Strong AI animation skills:** You can produce beautiful 3D cartoon-style animation using modern AI tools.

- **Visual storytelling:** You know how to translate spoken dialogue into interesting animated scenes rather than simply illustrating every word literally.

- **Understanding of viral content:** You understand hooks, pacing, retention, and what makes animated content engaging on social media.

- **Character consistency:** You can maintain characters, environments, and visual styles across multiple shots.

- **Cinematic animation:** You understand lighting, composition, camera movement, and expressive character animation.

- **Voiceover synchronization:** You know how to time visuals, scene changes, and animations naturally with existing audio.

- **Creative judgment:** You can independently d
 which visuals best support the message.

- **Attention to detail:** You recognize and correct distorted characters, awkward movements, and obvious AI artifacts.

- **Speed and efficiency:** You have a reliable workflow for consistently producing high-quality animated videos.

- **Strong communication:** You're responsive, organized, and comfortable working with feedback and revisions.



## AI Tools & Workflow



You should be experienced with AI image and video generation tools such as:



- Kling

- Runway

- Google Veo

- Sora

- Midjourney

- Nano Banana

We're not attached to any specific software.



**We care about the quality of your finished videos and your ability to produce them consistently.**

We're particularly interested in:



- Pixar-inspired 3D cartoon animation

- DreamWorks-style animated characters

- Expressive characters and engaging visual storytelling

- Cinematic lighting and imaginative environments

- Colorful, polished, professional-looking animation

- Short-form animation designed specifically for social media



The videos should feel like cohesive animated stories, not a collection of disconnected AI-generated scenes.

We have an existing library of successful scripts and voiceovers, so you won't need to develop every concept from scratch.

title: Content Clipper / Editor - Short-Form Social Media
description:
Do you want to work on content that reaches millions of people while being part of a fast-growing transformation and sound healing brand built around community?



Our content averages roughly **50–150 million views per month**, and we're looking for a highly skilled **Short-Form Content Clipper** to join our team full time.



We're expanding our long-form content production and need someone who can turn hours of footage into compelling, high-retention short-form videos for Instagram,
, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts.



**This is NOT a traditional video editing role.**



We're looking for someone who understands **viral content, the psychology of hooks, storytelling, pacing, and audience retention.**



The most important skill is knowing **what to clip, where to start, what to cut out, and exactly when to end.**



## About Us



Harmony is a fast-growing transformation, music, and sound healing company founded by musician and intuitive guide Banah Winn.



We create Golden Ratio Frequencies, guided experiences, educational content, live events, and an online community dedicated to helping people create meaningful change in their lives.



Our content reaches **50–150 million views per month**, and we're expanding into more long-form videos, live teachings, interviews, music performances, and behind-the-scenes documentaries.



We have an established creative team and a deep understanding of what performs on social media. We're looking for someone who can help us turn our growing library of long-form content into a consistent stream of powerful short-form videos.



## About the Role



Your main responsibility will be to **review long-form footage, independently identify the strongest moments, and turn them into engaging short-form clips.**



You won't always be given timestamps or instructions telling you what to cut. You'll need the judgment to recognize which moments have the highest potential to perform on social media.



Sometimes the best hook is buried in the middle of a conversation. Sometimes removing 20 seconds makes the entire clip more compelling. Sometimes a moment needs to breathe.



**Your ability to make these decisions is the core skill we're hiring for.**



## What You'll Be Clipping



We produce a variety of long-form content, including:



- **Vlogs & Behind-the-Scenes:** Interesting, funny, authentic, and emotional moments that tell a story.

- **Live Teaching & Authority Videos:** Powerful insights, explanations, and breakthroughs from webinars, live calls, and educational sessions.

- **Interviews & Conversations:** Surprising answers, compelling stories, memorable exchanges, and interesting perspectives.

- **Live Music & Performances:** Beautiful, moving, and engaging moments from live musical sessions.

- **Long-Form Talking Videos:** Strong teachings, memorable statements, and valuable explanations.

- **Guest Teachers & Community Calls:** Engaging moments from other guides, teachers, and community members.



Each format requires a different approach to selecting clips, storytelling, and pacing.



## What We're Looking For



- **Excellent understanding of viral hooks:** You know what stops someone from scrolling and how to capture attention in the first few seconds.

- **Strong editorial judgment:** You can identify the most compelling moments and know exactly where to start, what to remove, and when to end a clip.

- **Understanding of retention and pacing:** You recognize when content drags, when to make cuts, and when to let a moment breathe.

- **Excellent English comprehension:** You understand natural conversation, humor, emotion, nuance, and context well enough to recognize powerful moments.

- **Short-form storytelling:** You can turn longer conversations into standalone clips with a clear, engaging structure.

- **Knowledge of viral formats:** You actively study successful social media content and understand what makes different styles perform.

- **Strong editing fundamentals:** Clean cuts, natural dialogue, good audio, and proper vertical formatting.

- **Independence and efficiency:** You can review large amounts of footage, select clips, and deliver them quickly without constant direction.

- **Reliability and communication:** You consistently meet deadlines, communicate clearly, and work effectively within a team.



### Bonus Skills



- On-screen captions and text overlays

- Simple graphics and supporting visuals

- Experience growing social media accounts organically

- Proven clips with significant organic views

- Experience with music, podcasts, interviews, or documentary-style content



## Editing Style



Our style is generally **simple, clean, and native to social media.**



We're not looking for complicated effects, flashy transitions, or heavy motion graphics.



Initially, your focus will be on selecting great moments, making clean cuts, tightening pacing, and creating clips that keep people watching.



On-screen captions and text overlays are not required for every clip initially, but we'd ideally like someone who knows how to add them.



We care much more about **content selection and retention than complicated editing.**



## Speed & Volume



As our long-form production expands, we'll have a significant amount of footage to review.



We need someone who can work efficiently, identify the strongest moments, and consistently deliver high-quality clips.



This is intended to be a **full-time position** with consistent ongoing work and opportunities to grow with the company.



## Pay



**$8/hour**



## To Apply



Please send:



- **3–5 examples of your best short-form clips created from longer content**

- **The number of views each clip received and the platform it was posted on** (Instagram, TikTok,
, or YouTube Shorts)

- Links to the published clips so we can review them

- Your experience clipping long-form content

- Your typical turnaround time

- Your current availability

- Your earliest start date



**Please do not send only cinematic edits, music videos, motion graphics, or scripted talking-head videos.**



We want to see examples that demonstrate your ability to **find compelling moments in longer footage and turn them into engaging short-form content.**

title: AI Video Creator & Motion Editor (Higgsfield / Generative AI)
description:
Location: Remote / Tampa, FL



Job Type: Contract / Project-Based (with potential for ongoing campaign work)



Compensation: Competitive Project Rate / Hourly (DOE)



About the Role

Tribeca Atelier is seeking a skilled AI Video Creator and Post-Production Editor to help produce a serialized, animated commercial campaign promoting our upcoming flagship cosmetology academy.



We are developing a narrative episodic story centered on character development, salon craftsmanship, and high-end visual style. The visual benchmark blends a 2.5D painterly, gouache/oil illustrative aesthetic (reminiscent of Arcane) with dynamic, cinematic direction.



You will translate storyboard prompts and visual assets into consistent video scenes using generative AI motion platforms—specifically Higgsfield—and assemble them into polished, sound-designed marketing assets across digital and social formats.



Key Responsibilities

Generative Motion & Video Synthesis: Direct, generate, and iterate motion shots using Higgsfield (leveraging character training models, camera control, and reference-guided generation) to achieve smooth, expressive movement without uncanny distortions.



Character & Aesthetic Consistency: Maintain strict visual and character model continuity across multi-scene narrative arcs based on established 2D/2.5D visual keys.



Editing & Post-Production: Cut, sequence, and pace scenes inside Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or Final Cut Pro; assemble multi-chapter vignettes tailored for web and short-form vertical video (9:16 and 16:9).



AI Cleanup & Inpainting: Perform frame interpolation, inpainting, cleanup, upscaling (e.g., Topaz), and stabilization to resolve common AI motion artifacts or limb inconsistencies.



Sound Design & Finishing: Integrate voiceover tracks, custom ambient Foley (salon sounds, urban ambiance), royalty-free cinematic scoring, and typography/motion graphics for titles and calls to action.



What We Are Looking For

Demonstrated AI Video Fluency: Hands-on experience executing end-to-end clips using Higgsfield (alongside platforms like Midjourney, Runway Gen-3, or Luma Dream Machine) with an understanding of seed consistency, camera prompts, and character anchors.



Strong Traditional Filmmaking & Editing Fundamentals: Deep knowledge of pacing, blocking, focal lengths, match cuts, and color grading.



Stylistic Eye: Ability to steer and preserve stylized, painterly aesthetics (avoiding generic "glossy 3D CGI" or synthetic stock appearances).



Portfolio / Reel Required: A reel demonstrating generative AI motion clips integrated with sound design, continuity across multiple cuts, and clean frame-to-frame movement.



Preferred Qualifications

Experience with character training/LoRAs or fine-tuned model workflows.



Familiarity with beauty, fashion, editorial hair styling, or design-forward brand storytelling.



Proficiency in After Effects for motion graphics, title sequences, and subtle visual compositing.



How to Apply

Please submit your portfolio or showreel highlighting:



Examples of AI-generated video workflows where character or stylistic consistency is maintained across multiple cuts.



An outline of your primary toolstack (specifying your experience with Higgsfield).



Your standard project turnaround time and contract/hourly rates.

title: News Lead Editor – Health & Medical News (Remote)
description:
We are looking for an experienced, highly driven Lead Editor to oversee health and medical news coverage for Medical Daily UK.



This is a hands-on leadership role for an editor who can balance traffic growth with exceptional standards for accuracy, responsible reporting, originality, and editorial quality. You will lead writers, shape the daily news agenda, identify high-potential stories, and ensure every article is informative, engaging, trustworthy, and valuable to readers.



You should understand what makes health and medical news perform online, how to identify emerging health trends and important research developments, and how to turn complex medical information into clear, accessible, and compelling articles for a broad audience.



What You'll Do



Lead the editorial team during your shift and maintain a strong, consistent flow of health and medical news coverage.

Identify high-interest health and medical stories with strong traffic potential, particularly in medical breakthroughs, diseases, treatments, public health, mental health, nutrition, fitness, wellness, pharmaceuticals, and scientific research.

Monitor breaking health news, medical studies, research publications, public health announcements, healthcare developments, competitor coverage, search trends, and online conversations for story opportunities.

Develop fresh, compelling, and reader-focused angles that explain why health and medical developments matter to everyday readers.

Create and refine engaging, SEO-friendly headlines designed to perform across Google Search, Google Discover, MSN, Reddit, and other traffic platforms without exaggerating medical claims.

Edit articles rigorously for medical accuracy, originality, clarity, structure, sourcing, context, and readability.

Fact-check medical claims, research findings, clinical studies, statistics, treatment information, and expert commentary before publication.

Ensure writers distinguish between scientifically established evidence, preliminary research, correlation, and causation.

Ensure articles are supported by credible medical sources, peer-reviewed studies, recognised health organisations, and qualified experts whenever appropriate.

Monitor article performance, identify traffic opportunities, and adjust headlines, story angles, and coverage strategies accordingly.

Assign stories, manage deadlines, and ensure writers consistently meet editorial and productivity expectations.

Coach writers to improve their research, medical fact-checking, headline writing, storytelling, and understanding of digital audience behaviour.

Maintain high editorial standards while ensuring timely coverage of breaking medical news and trending health topics.

What We're Looking For



We're looking for someone with strong editing and newsroom leadership experience, preferably in health journalism, medical reporting, science journalism, digital publishing, or online news media.



You should have a solid understanding of health and medical topics, scientific research, public health issues, healthcare developments, and emerging wellness trends.



The ideal candidate should be able to identify stories with strong readership potential, develop competitive headlines, and make quick editorial decisions without compromising medical accuracy, responsible reporting, or quality.



You should also have:



Proven experience as a Lead Editor, Senior Editor, News Editor, Health Editor, or similar editorial leadership role.

Excellent English writing, editing, grammar, and fact-checking skills.

Strong knowledge of SEO, Google Discover, MSN, Reddit, and digital audience development.

Experience managing writers, assigning stories, and maintaining publishing schedules.

Ability to identify trending health topics, breaking medical developments, and stories with strong traffic potential.

Strong understanding of credible medical sources, clinical studies, scientific research, and evidence-based reporting.

Ability to critically evaluate medical claims, research findings, and health information before publication.

Strong editorial judgement and the ability to work efficiently under tight deadlines.

Familiarity with content management systems, particularly WordPress, is an advantage.

Ability to work independently and manage a remote editorial team.

For Medical Daily UK, traffic growth is important, but medical accuracy, responsible reporting, originality, editorial quality, and reader trust must always remain a priority.



Working Hours



Monday to Friday



4:00 PM – 12:00 Midnight (Philippine Time)



This is a remote position requiring consistent availability throughout the assigned shift, including weekends.



Probationary Period



This role is subject to an initial probationary period. During this time, we will assess editorial judgement, medical accuracy, sourcing standards, leadership, team management, traffic performance, productivity, and overall fit before confirming the successful candidate in the Lead Editor position.



To Apply



Please submit your CV and relevant writing or editing samples, preferably demonstrating experience in health journalism, medical reporting, science journalism, or digital news publishing.



Shortlisted candidates may be required to complete a brief editing, medical fact-checking, headline writing, and news judgement exercise as part of the selection process.



Benefits



Work from home

Fully remote working environment

Opportunity to lead a growing digital newsroom

Exposure to international health and medical news and digital publishing

title: Backlink Specialist / Off-Page SEO Specialist
description:
About the Role



You will be responsible for planning, executing, and managing backlink-building strategies across approximately 10 client websites.



This is a specialist position focused primarily on off-page SEO and link acquisition. We are looking for someone who understands what makes a backlink valuable, knows how to secure quality links, and can demonstrate how their work contributes to improved search visibility and rankings.



You will also be expected to monitor campaign performance, prepare reports, and communicate progress and strategies to clients when required.



Key Skills and Experience

- Proven experience specialising in backlink building and off-page SEO.

- Strong portfolio demonstrating successful link-building campaigns and measurable results.

- Expertise in acquiring high-quality, relevant backlinks from authoritative websites.

- Hands-on experience with guest posting, niche edits, link outreach, digital PR, and other legitimate link acquisition strategies.

- Ability to conduct competitor backlink analysis and identify quality link-building opportunities.

- Strong understanding of domain authority, referring domains, anchor text distribution, link relevance, and backlink quality.

- Experience identifying and assessing toxic or potentially harmful backlinks.

- Ability to develop tailored backlink strategies for different industries and business types.

- Proficient in Ahrefs, Semrush, Majestic or similar backlink analysis tools.

- Experience managing multiple websites and campaigns simultaneously.

- Strong analytical skills with the ability to track, measure, and report backlink performance.

- Fluent English with strong written and verbal communication skills.

- Comfortable working independently, managing priorities, and taking ownership of tasks.



Work Hours

- Full-time, 40 hours per week.

- Monday to Friday, weekends off.

- Must be available during ACST business hours (Adelaide, Australia).



Contract and Pay

- Immediate start.

- 6-month contract with possibility to renew.

- Pay: AUD 1,500 per month.



Application Requirements

To be considered, applicants MUST submit all three of the following:



1. Updated CV/Resume – Include your relevant SEO experience, particularly your background in backlink building and off-page SEO.



2. Proof of Backlink Expertise – Provide actual evidence of your backlink-building experience. This may include:

   - Examples of websites you have built backlinks for.

   - Backlink campaign reports or screenshots from Ahrefs, Semrush or similar tools.

   - Case studies showing improvements in referring domains, backlink quality, organic rankings, or website authority.

   - Examples of successful link acquisition campaigns and websites where you secured backlinks.

   - A brief explanation of your link-building strategies and the results achieved.



3. Short Loom Video (2–3 minutes) – Introduce yourself and explain your backlink-building expertise. Discuss your experience, the strategies you use to acquire quality backlinks, and examples of measurable results you have achieved.



Important: All three application requirements are mandatory. Applications missing even one of these submissions will be archived and will not proceed to the screening stage.

You provide the continuous security monitoring and i
-response support that a lean IT team cannot sustain alongside daily operations. You watch identity and access activity, execute hardening to defined standards, run access reviews, and act as a second responder during i

Execute Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and Conditional Access hardening to defined standards; maintain authentication-method policies. 

Run access recertifications and reviews; identify stale, excessive, or orphaned access. 

Serve as second responder during security i
: triage, containment steps, evidence gathering, documentation, and coordination. 

Maintain security reporting and dashboards; track remediation items to closure. 

Support audit and compliance evidence collection. 



Required qualifications:

2+ years in a SOC, security operations, or IAM-security role. 

Working knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID security: Conditional Access, MFA, sign-in and audit logs, and Identity Protection concepts, plus Microsoft 365 security basics. 

Understanding of i
-response fundamentals and least-privilege / access-review practices. 

Strong documentation, clear written English, and discretion with sensitive data. 



Nice to have:

title: Telemarketer
description:
B2B Appointment Setter & List Researcher — long-term, remote, paid hourly



THE ROLE



You call small and mid-sized businesses in Western Canada (BC and Alberta) and book short intro meetings between the person in charge of their employee benefits plan and our advisor. You are not selling insurance — you're booking a 30-minute conversation. A full operations manual, proven script and objection responses are provided.



Our clients tell us they stay with us for three things: sustainable rate savings, clarity in their coverage (no surprises at claim time), and an advisor who responds quickly, is patient, and acts in their best interest. Your call is a prospect's first taste of that experience — every call should sound like it.



This job is two jobs, and we value them equally:



-Calling (the visible half): friendly, unhurried cold calls during Pacific/Mountain business hours — gatekeepers, decision makers, objections, and booking meetings via Calendly.

-Research & data (the hidden half): verifying phone numbers and decision makers on company websites, enriching new lists before dialing, and keeping meticulous dated notes in our spreadsheet. The first pass through any new list is mostly cleanup — that is expected, and it's exactly why we pay by the hour, not per call.



YOU'RE A FIT IF



-Your spoken English is fluent and natural — you sound like a friendly colleague, not a script reader.

-You're meticulous: every dial logged the moment you hang up, dates as YYYY-MM-DD, notes a stranger could pick up and continue from.

-You're patient and steady — you'd rather build clean data and 3–6 solid meetings a week than burn through a list for volume.

-You're honest on the phone: comfortable saying “good question — that's exactly what the meeting is for” instead of bluffing.

-You want one long-term client and are reliably available during Canadian business hours.



YOU'RE NOT A FIT IF



-You're paid-per-call minded: maximum dials, minimum notes, next gig.

-You find the research/data-entry half of the work beneath you.

-Your style is pressure, exaggeration, or arguing past a “no.”



THE ONE NON-NEGOTIABLE



You are our brand to every person you reach. Protecting the brand outranks any single meeting: courteous, honest, zero pressure, on every call. “Don't call again” is honoured forever. If a call turns sour, exit politely and log it.



WHAT WE PROVIDE



A complete operations manual with scripts and objection handling, a researched call list, spreadsheet conventions, Calendly for booking, and regular debriefs and coaching directly with the principal. We invest in one caller who gets better every month.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE



First two weeks: list enriched, script comfortable in your own words. Steady state: 100–150 dials a day, 15–25 real decision-maker conversations, 3–6 booked meetings a week — and a spreadsheet that's always current. Meetings booked and data quality are what we measure; dials are just how you get there.



HOW TO APPLY



Please don't send a resume or reply here — send a short video (2–3 minutes). Introduce yourself, tell us about your calling and research experience, and speak to us the way you'd speak to a business owner on a Tuesday morning. Then, so we know you actually read this page, finish your video by telling us the three things our clients say they stay with us for. Videos that skip that last part won't be considered — attention to detail is the job.



Upload video here:
